articles.coveralt: A photo of Tucker, one of the LGBTQ students featured in this story, backlit against the light of a stained glass window, at church.

articles.headline: Records of Reflection
articles.author: Mattie Sanseverino
articles.excerpt: Students highlight unconventional memoirs of personal growth, from online shopping carts and closet space to the nominal records of their musical endeavors.
articles.coveralt: An illustration of Mattie, the writer, smiling at the art posters hanging on her wall. Small lights are hanging above her head.

articles.headline: Traveling Thoughts
articles.author: Clea Wurster
articles.excerpt: On a quest to define her identity as a city dweller, one writer discusses how public transportation may be key to connecting Bruins to Los Angeles.
articles.coveralt: An illustration of the writer, Clea Wurster, riding the Berlin metro and looking out of the window at the city. She is surrounded by other commuters who are busy going about their day, some watching the time and others reading or on their phones.

articles.headline: Walking the Bruin Walk
articles.author: Keshav Tadimeti
articles.excerpt: The personal stories and missions that led Andre Oliver and Saul Marquez — two of Bruin Walk's most notable personalities — to UCLA's campus.
articles.coveralt: A photo of Andre Oliver sitting in a chair in the center of Bruin Walk, UCLA students walking in the background. He is looking to his right, and he is covering his hand with his chin.

articles.headline: Recipes for Remembering
articles.author: Pauline Ordonez
articles.excerpt: Glimpses into the evolution of one writer's understanding of food as it fosters a sense of  belonging, identity, and remembrance.
articles.coveralt: An illustration of food laid out on a counter. Clockwise starting from left corner: atchara pickles, rafute pork, goya, green onions, Okinawan sweet potato, rice, banana leaves, and calamansi.

articles.headline: Apathy in the Stands
articles.author: Anush Khatri
articles.excerpt: Investigating UCLA Athletics' falling attendance numbers, a writer explores the factors pulling fans away from the stands.
articles.coveralt: An illustration of an empty Pauley Pavilion. Blue light shines into the stadium from an open door to the far right of the image.

articles.headline: Destigmatizing Dependency
articles.author: Axel Lopez
articles.excerpt: Students share experiences with drug misuse, highlighting how stigma often stands in the way of recovery from dependency and addiction.
articles.coveralt: An image of a student obscuring his face with his hand. He is holding a lighter and is facing a grinder containing ground-up marijuana.

articles.headline: I Miss the Old Kanye
articles.author: MacKenzie Coffman
articles.excerpt: Uncovering the psychological processes driving contradicting sentiments that arise from supporting an artist in spite of controversy.
articles.coveralt: An illustration of Kanye West surrounded by imagery relating to his past albums including “Graduation” and “Yeezus.” He is wearing a “Make America Great Again” hat.

articles.headline: Tuning the Mind
articles.author: Polina Cherezova
articles.excerpt: The more I cared about performing well, the more I would become frustrated with my inability to silence the noisy critic living inside my head.
articles.coveralt: A photo of Polina resting her head over her folded arms, on a piano.

articles.headline: Sống sót  / Survival
articles.author: Kristie-Valerie Hoang
articles.excerpt: Despite being born in different countries and eras, both generations engaged and continue to engage in survival.

articles.headline: From the Road to Royce
articles.author: John Tudhope
articles.excerpt: This ex-roadie knows that his life has been uniquely shaped by his experiences working alongside some of rock music’s most legendary acts.

articles.headline: Slowing the Storm
articles.author: Hanna Rashidi
articles.excerpt: There are places and people who change us immeasurably, quietly, without us noticing, until we look up one rainy day and realize that they were the compass that guided us. These are the memories I want with me when I leave.

articles.headline: Fighting for Home
articles.author: Susana Alcantar
articles.excerpt: While the uncertainty surrounding the Obama-era program remains intact, DACA recipients at UCLA remain firm in their willingness to advocate for their own futures.

articles.headline: The Dead are Alive at UCLA
articles.author: John Tudhope
articles.excerpt: Since his first Grateful Dead show, the band’s music has taken Tudhope across the nation on some strange trips and given me incredibly intense and joyful experiences. He has been happy to discover that many Bruins, young and old, have had their lives changed as well.

articles.headline: Camera Confidence
articles.author: Bilal Ismail Ahmed
articles.excerpt: Although talking to the camera first seemed like a substitute for talking to other people, it gave Ahmed the confidence to start up a conversation about anything.

articles.headline: Third Culture Kids
articles.author: Hedy Wang
articles.excerpt: Third culture kids are individuals who have grown up in one or multiple countries other than their parents’ or their own country of citizenship. When I spoke with other third culture kids at UCLA, I found they too have dealt with the inevitability of change in our lives, from lost friendships to places we call home.

articles.headline: Many Tribes, One People
articles.author: Madeleine Pauker
articles.excerpt: Each spring, UCLA’s American Indian Student Association hosts a two-day pow wow, drawing hundreds of Native Americans to celebrate their cultures and compete in different dance events.

articles.headline: Pub Peeves
articles.author: William Thorne
articles.excerpt: Thorne wasn’t expecting to find bang-up pubs 5,000 miles away from his homeland, but the couple of pubs that he has visited in Los Angeles have boasted more TV screens than the NSA control room and more options on the menu than any patron could possibly comprehend.

articles.headline: First in the Family
articles.author: Axel Lopez
articles.excerpt: Being a first-gen college student means more than being the first in your family to attend and complete a degree at a four-year university. First-gen undergraduates at UCLA share an incredibly difficult, yet rewarding experience.

articles.headline: A Change of Plan
articles.author: Angela Song
articles.excerpt: Inspired by my parents, Angela Song believed that as long as she worked hard and did well in class, she would fulfill her dream. That was the plan, but reality is much more complicated.

articles.headline: LA’s Filipino Foodscape
articles.author: Catherine Liberty Feliciano
articles.excerpt: People are saying it’s (Filipinos’) time,” Baluyot said. “My response is, ‘It’s about time.’” Here’s a snapshot of what some of Los Angeles’ newer Filipino restaurants have to offer.
